searchText: Hello pandas, what would be an effective path to test attestation deadline at 2 seconds instead of 3? change the % in the config all of these are exposed under network_params in kurtosis you will have to change everything else too, as everything is % point now dependent on what you want for the other values, adjust `attestation_due_bps_gloas: 1666` and increase the aggregate or whatever else what is the goal here? in a non-6s context Testing in these single server devnets it's a first step but only to find out if we're screwed from the start. <@654267572107083777> the broadcast time up to the attestation deadline becomes effectively useless time of the slot in ePBS. By lowering it we can lower the payload timelines check. Guaranteeing the same execution/proving time without removing the Payload broadcast time. This also allows us to squeeze more from timing games and also reduces the UX deficit of delaying tx inclusion for the time between CL block availability and EL block availability Do we wanna touch changing these times in gloas? I'd actually hold off and just leave everything as is, and iterate further on slot restructuring in the following fork. I'm a bit afraid that we won't have too much gain unless we shorten the slot time i think potuz isnt proposing changing the slot time but just when the attestation deadline occurs at to reduce dead time in the slot I think this is reasonable, specially for PTC deadlines like dual deadlines. But attestation deadline is a little trickier cause it will have to be a hard fork to change it, so I would rather pick the right one now. Specially since the block size will not change at all with gas limit So it makes sense to get it right. That's consistent with this though, no? The counter-proposal here is not to do this in Gloas, but to do this as part of a broader look at slot restructuring in the next hardfork There are a lot of things it "makes sense to get" right, but there's a limited amount it makes sense to change each hardfork yeah I'd just stick to the current values, even if we have a ton of deadtime and figure out the right times in heze Problem is that at 3 seconds deadline and 6 second PTC payload deadline, it gives only 2 seconds for Payload broadcast. This seems already tight for 200M gas. So leaving the attestation deadline at 3" will force us to move PTC dual deadline to after 6 seconds which will effectively cap gas limit to prevent the block from executing into the next slot (something we can't really handle at forkchoice). In other words, if we keep numbers as exactly speced right now, we cannot allow a gas limit that takes 3 seconds to execute Thus we can't handle 200M as promised heze will make it more complicated with FOCIL, so I think we should figure out good values now > This seems already tight for 200M gas. 200M gas is an aspirational goal inasmuch as 100M gas was an aspirational goal last year. It's nice if it happens, yeah. And it can/should guide some decisions. But it's not a commitment in the same sense as a concrete EIP This is not to say anything against it, but the process for deciding 200M was ... not very rigorous. And it's suspiciously a big round number There was no 200M promise, at least no more than there was a 100M promise. That did not happen, and that's ok I'm being a bit directly here because I want to avoid the semantic drift from "By Friday, the three threads converged on the headline number for the week: a credible 200M post-Glamsterdam gas limit floor." to a "promise" here I disagree, we can easily do much more now, we have a lot of slack, we don't do it just because we aren't enforcing better timings. I don't want to stress the nodes, I just want to measure what we can do comfortably So as an example, we can simply go from 3 seconds to 6 seconds by just moving the PTC to dual deadlines, no hard fork, no nothing "aspirational" doesn't mean "unachievable" I'm trying to be fairly precise. It is and always was a handwavy number. _Literally_ handwavy Yes, it comes from somewhere, I know I think we are more or less on the same boat, to have something less handwavy we need benches, and that's what I am asking for Ok, the core/only point, and I really don't want to spam too much more, is the idea that 200M is a "promise". That's really all these last few messages of mine are addressing. excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Testing in these single server devnets it's a first step but only to find out if we're screwed from the start.

<@654267572107083777> the broadcast time up to the attestation deadline becomes effectively useless time of the slot in ePBS. By lowering it we can lower the payload timelines check. Guaranteeing the same execution/proving time without removing the Payload broadcast time. This also allows us to squeeze more from timing games and also reduces the UX deficit of delaying tx inclusion for the time between CL block availability and EL block availability

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: Do we wanna touch changing these times in gloas? I'd actually hold off and just leave everything as is, and iterate further on slot restructuring in the following fork. I'm a bit afraid that we won't have too much gain unless we shorten the slot time

excerpts.content: i think potuz isnt proposing changing the slot time but just when the attestation deadline occurs at

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content: to reduce dead time in the slot

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think this is reasonable, specially for PTC deadlines like dual deadlines. But attestation deadline is a little trickier cause it will have to be a hard fork to change it, so I would rather pick the right one now. Specially since the block size will not change at all with gas limit

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: So it makes sense to get it right.

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: That's consistent with this though,  no? The counter-proposal here is not to do this in Gloas, but to do this as part of a broader look at slot restructuring in the next hardfork

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: There are a lot of things it "makes sense to get" right, but there's a limited amount it makes sense to change each hardfork

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: yeah I'd just stick to the current values, even if we have a ton of deadtime

excerpts.author: barnabasbusa
excerpts.content: and figure out the right times in heze

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Problem is that at 3 seconds deadline and 6 second PTC payload deadline, it gives only 2 seconds for Payload broadcast. This seems already tight for 200M gas. So leaving the attestation deadline at 3" will force us to move PTC dual deadline to after 6 seconds which will effectively cap gas limit to prevent the block from executing into the next slot (something we can't really handle at forkchoice).

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: In other words, if we keep numbers as exactly speced right now, we cannot allow a gas limit that takes 3 seconds to execute

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: Thus we can't handle 200M as promised

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: heze will make it more complicated with FOCIL, so I think we should figure out good values now

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content:
> This seems already tight for 200M gas.

200M gas is an aspirational goal inasmuch as 100M gas was an aspirational goal last year. It's nice if it happens, yeah. And it can/should guide some decisions. But it's not a commitment in the same sense as a concrete EIP

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: This is not to say anything against it, but the process for deciding 200M was ... not very rigorous. And it's suspiciously a big round number

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: There was no 200M promise, at least no more than there was a 100M promise. That did not happen, and that's ok

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: I'm being a bit directly here because I want to avoid the semantic drift from "By Friday, the three threads converged on the headline number for the week: a credible 200M post-Glamsterdam gas limit floor." to a "promise"

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: here I disagree, we can easily do much more now, we have a lot of slack, we don't do it just because we aren't enforcing better timings. I don't want to stress the nodes, I just want to measure what we can do comfortably

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: So as an example, we can simply go from 3 seconds to 6 seconds by just moving the PTC to dual deadlines, no hard fork, no nothing

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: "aspirational" doesn't mean "unachievable"

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: I'm trying to be fairly precise. It is and always was a handwavy number. _Literally_ handwavy

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Yes, it comes from somewhere, I know

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I think we are more or less on the same boat, to have something less handwavy we need benches, and that's what I am asking for

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Ok, the core/only point, and I really don't want to spam too much more, is the idea that 200M is a "promise". That's really all these last few messages of mine are addressing. It simply is not

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: It's "credible"

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: This isn't to disagree with scaling as some general idea, it's to say 200M isn't a magic threshold

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: broadly, sure

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: that's fine, I'm only using these numbers as "what we can do now", today with 3 seconds we can't do much more than 60M, if we merge https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5212 then we get much more (whatever benches give for 6 seconds execution), and if we move the attestation deadline to 2 seconds then we get also more stability in the happy case.
